title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that compares ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline applied to a single shared LLM candidate per intent. Generation used gpt-5-mini and the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We report auditable descriptions of the validator and repair operator, execution accounting (model_calls_used = 201; deterministic repair invocations = 1), explicit diagnostics about statistical sensitivity given the observed discordant counts (n = 1), and limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises an operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work demonstrates intent-to-configuration prototypes and documents structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. Despite these proposals, there is limited execution-grounded evidence that quantifies the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate (a low-hosted-call operational estimand).

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the "repair-on-same-candidate" question by sharing a single initial LLM candidate across both arms (baseline ungated acceptance and guarded generate–verify–repair). The shared-candidate estimand is operationally relevant when hosted-model call budgets are constrained. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete execution accounting and exact-test justification for small-discordant-pair inference.
sections.related_work:
Research exploring LLMs for NetOps has produced three interlocking strands that motivate the present study. First, intent-to-configuration work demonstrates that LLMs can synthesize device CLI-like commands from natural-language intents but that structured-output errors are common without additional constraints (missing required commands, incorrect ordering, or violation of protected-field policies). Empirical intent-translation prototypes and surveys document these failure modes and report prototype success under curated conditions (Nguyen et al., 2024) [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. Complementary surveys and architectural analyses (Bilal et al., 2026) characterize the operator-facing requirements—auditability, bounded tool use, and verifier integration—needed for operational adoption.

Second, mitigation approaches have emerged from adjacent domains. Retrieval-augmented generation, live schema grounding, and constrained decoding reduce hallucination in NL2SQL and document-grounded tasks; grammar/constrained decoding methods (e.g., Geng et al., 2023) show enforcing syntactic/schema constraints at decode-time reduces format errors without model fine-tuning. Deterministic validators and emulator-backed checks have also been proposed to reduce high-stakes hallucinations.

Third, deterministic formal verification (NetKAT variants and ensemble verifiers) can check reachability and isolation properties and are natural candidates for validators in generated-configuration workflows (Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026) [doi:10.1145/3808318]. However, verification has limits: control-plane dynamics (e.g., BGP convergence) and vendor idiosyncrasies are not always captured by static checks. Generate–verify–repair architectures are therefore a pragmatic pattern; our study provides a preregistered, execution-grounded measure of the marginal yield when repairs are deterministic and applied only to the shared initial candidate (a low-call operational budget).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: We preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration which was then scored directly as the baseline arm and also passed, unchanged, to the guarded arm. The guarded arm applied a deterministic validator; when the validator reported a repairable violation the pipeline invoked a deterministic, rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤ 1, no additional LLM calls). The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); the preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). The execution environment combined Dockerized Mininet+FRR with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the canonical validator.

Task bank and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs generated deterministically. Each task payload includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, workflow policies (make-before-break, minimum-active constraints, protected interfaces), and difficulty metadata. Scoring requires that generated configurations (a) parse syntactically, (b) include the task’s required_sequence (presence and order), (c) respect dependency/group policies, (d) preserve protected-interface values, and (e) produce the emulator-observed expected_final_state when applied in the deterministic emulator. Provider/API generation failures are treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred in the confirmatory run.

Deterministic validator: The validator executes three ordered stages and emits a machine-readable trace used by scoring and repair logic. Stage 1 — syntactic parsing and canonical normalization: tokenizes CLI-like lines and produces normalized_configuration; syntax failures yield SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR and are unrepaired. Stage 2 — structural and workflow checks: verifies presence and ordering of required_sequence entries and enforces dependency and group policies; it emits deterministic violation codes (MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION). Stage 3 — deterministic emulator application: normalized_configuration is applied to the emulator to produce observed final_state, and validation_after.valid is true only if observed final_state equals expected_final_state. Per-episode validator traces (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, violation_count, violation_codes, validation_before/after summaries) are archived for audit.

Repair operator: The preregistered repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based transformer invoked only when (i) validator.violation_count > 0 and (ii) the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set with a unique mapping to a deterministic transformation given the task manifest. The operator consults required_sequence, initial_state, expected_final_state, and workflow_policies (all from the task manifest) and implements three canonical deterministic transformations: (a) Insertion: insert missing commands present in task required_sequence at canonical positions; (b) Reordering: perform minimal stable reordering of contiguous command blocks to satisfy dependency constraints; (c) Preservation enforcement: replace offending commands that modify protected fields with canonical preserved values from initial_state or expected_final_state. Ambiguous or multi-candidate repairs cause abstention (no change) and are flagged as nonrepairable. All repair decisions and resulting normalized_configuration are recorded in a repair trace archived with the run artifacts. In this confirmatory run the deterministic repair operator was invoked exactly once and converted that episode to a validator pass.

Aggregate task-difficulty recording: Each task in the confirmatory bank is labeled with a difficulty.level string (e.g., easy, medium, hard, very_hard) in the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). The manifest contains the full per-task difficulty labels and is the authoritative record for difficulty stratification; the manifest is archived as part of the evidence bundle and supports reproduction and any aggregated counting or stratified reanalysis by readers.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level artifact-backed counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv; SHA-256: 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256: 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI details: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) was computed on the observed discordant count n = n10 + n01 = 1; the resulting two-sided p-value reported by the analysis executor is p = 1.0 (analysis/results.json; input_results_sha256: e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding a 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256: aa1147b793eb71be336f715f6078a1d676ddbd9f7d10ca95bfe74fa4b5bfbf3d). Because the preregistered primary effect-size target (absolute 0.15) lies well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude of improvement under the shared-candidate estimand.

Repair and failure-accounting diagnostics: The validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and the single deterministic repair converted that episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256: 59a3745f3504467e3433968928a83e63f73d4ea2f481cee294e7935221700055 and execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}.

Artifact-grounded exemplar of the single repaired episode: The complete per-episode records (validator trace, repair trace, and before/after normalized configurations) are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58) and the repair trace is captured in the same raw-results bundle. The archived record for the repaired episode includes: the episode task identifier, the validator.violation_codes reported before repair, the deterministic repair rule applied (one of insertion/reordering/preservation as described above), the normalized_configuration before repair, and the normalized_configuration after repair. Readers can inspect the exact JSON entry at execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 as above) to see the task id, the concrete violation codes, the canonical repair rule name, and the pre/post configuration strings; these archived fields are the authoritative, auditable record that supports the paired counts reported above.

Representative exemplars and difficulty context: To illustrate task difficulty and typical intents we publish six representative exemplars with validator traces and difficulty annotations in the evidence bundle (manuscript artifact examples). The exemplars include medium, hard, and very_hard patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make-before-break uplink switchover, paired atomic-MTU changes, safe-access/service-transfer, and rolling migration patterns. The full per-task difficulty label list for all 200 confirmatory intents is archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) for readers who require aggregate or stratified counts; the manifest is the authoritative source for any difficulty-level aggregation or further stratified analysis.

Interpretation of the small-discordant outcome: With only one discordant pair (n = 1), the exact McNemar test conveys that the observed marginal improvement (one converted episode) is not unlikely under the null in two-sided terms; the paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] quantifies the scale of uncertainty around the paired difference. Practically, deterministic repair-on-the-same-candidate delivered an auditable, low-cost correction in exactly one case in this curated confirmatory bank. In higher-error regimes or under alternative estimands (e.g., independent-resampling) the repair yield and statistical sensitivity could differ substantially.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation and practitioner guidance: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic, auditable validators produce structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in low-error regimes the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate; for contexts prioritizing maximal success, independent-resampling or LLM-invoked iterative repair are viable alternatives at greater provider cost.

Statistical-power clarification: The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline ≈0.5 and targeted an absolute improvement of 0.15 at n = 200. The observed baseline (0.995) compresses the set of possible discordant outcomes and thus substantially reduces achievable discordant counts under the paired estimand, shrinking statistical sensitivity for a 0.15 absolute improvement. Concretely, the observed discordant total was n = n10 + n01 = 1; with only one discordant pair the exact two-sided McNemar p-value is uninformative for rejecting small two-sided nulls and the bootstrap CI bound (upper = 0.015) formalizes that large preregistered effects are inconsistent with the observed data. Put differently, the near-ceiling baseline substantially limited the confirmatory power to detect large absolute improvements under this design; larger discordant counts (more baseline errors) or an independent-resampling estimand would be required to evaluate larger effect sizes with the same sample size.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring; construct validity depends on emulator fidelity—our deterministic emulator captures many stateful correctness conditions but cannot fully model runtime phenomena such as BGP convergence timing or vendor firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by one LLM (gpt-5-mini), the synthetic curated bank focused on small changes, and absence of adversarial or malformed intents in the confirmatory set. Conclusion validity is constrained by the observed near-ceiling baseline and the resulting small discordant count; we therefore treat the primary confirmatory outcome as evidence that in this curated, low-error regime deterministic guards produce low marginal yield but provide auditable assurance rather than as broad evidence for all NetOps workloads.

Reproducibility and auditability: All artifacts needed for reanalysis are archived in the evidence bundle: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: e3bb0089bb742517e662dd434db4a44e2f0f6b5f1da8b3151a309a7a6d5a3a58), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a), model configuration JSON (SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), and analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256: 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; condition_summary.csv SHA-256: 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a). The single repaired episode’s validator and repair traces can be inspected directly in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 above) to see the task id, violation_codes, canonical repair rule applied (insertion/reordering/preservation), and the pre/post normalized_configuration strings.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and task distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded negligible marginal improvement, but deterministic validators provide auditable assurance gates that are valuable in operational NetOps pipelines. All artifacts for inspection and reanalysis are archived in the evidence bundle; readers can inspect per-episode validator and repair traces to reproduce the single repaired episode’s before/after configurations and the full per-task difficulty labeling (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a).

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle (noted artifact paths and SHA-256 values appear in the manuscript).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the archived evidence bundle (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a); the manuscript references that manifest rather than enumerating the full 200-line distribution inline to preserve concise presentation while preserving auditable reproducibility.
